name: ecs-rollback
description: Puts an Amazon ECS service back on an earlier revision of its task definition, through the ECS API. It changes only the task definition: the service starts a new deployment of the older revision. The older revision is the ACTIVE revision of the same task definition family, below the one the service runs, that the service deployed successfully most recently, or the one revisionsBack such revisions down. A revision the service never deployed is not chosen: ECS keeps about 90 days of deployment history, and a revision that is INACTIVE cannot be deployed. When ECS has no deployment history for the service, or Sidekick may not read it, the highest ACTIVE revision below the one the service runs is used instead, and the proposal says so: check its image in the proposal. It works only for services on the ECS deployment controller. Accounts: 111122223333. Regions: us-east-1. Clusters: quillcart-prod. Services: order-intake, notify-*. revisionsBack is at most 1.

account.description: The 12-digit AWS account ID. It may be left out when the action works in only one account.

cluster.description: The name of the ECS cluster.

region.description: The AWS Region, for example us-east-1. It may be left out when the action works in only one Region.

revisionsBack.description: How many earlier task definition revisions of the service's family, that the service deployed and are ACTIVE, to go back from the one it runs. Default 1.

service.description: The name of the ECS service.
